title: Lipschitz sum invariance bound
statement: There is a constant $K>0$ such that for every natural number $n$, every two probability spaces, and independent real-valued families $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ and $Y_1,\ldots,Y_n$ on those respective spaces, the following holds whenever each variable has finite third absolute moment and corresponding variables have equal means and equal second moments. For every $c\ge0$ and every function $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ that is Lipschitz with constant at most $c$, the absolute difference between the expectations of $\psi(\sum_iX_i)$ and $\psi(\sum_iY_i)$ is at most $Kc\bigl(\sum_i(\mathbb E|X_i|^3+\mathbb E|Y_i|^3)\bigr)^{1/3}$.
hypotheses_covered: Both underlying spaces carry probability measures
Each $X_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Each $Y_i$ has finite third absolute moment
Corresponding variables have equal second moments
$\psi$ is Lipschitz with constant at most $c$
